goals.statement: Dispatchers monitor temperature integrity during transit to trigger corrective action on thermal excursions.

grounding.quote: Our dispatchers must monitor temperature integrity so excursions trigger immediate corrective action.

acceptable_paraphrases: Dispatch monitors reefer temperature to respond promptly to temperature deviations.

goals.statement: The logistics system re-routes freight vehicles to nearby authorized repair depots when refrigeration units fail.

grounding.quote: the system needs to re-route the truck to the nearest authorized refrigeration repair depot.

acceptable_paraphrases: Redirect compromised refrigerated trucks to certified service centers.

goals.statement: Remote telemetry hardware automatically disables vehicle ignition upon critical thermal excursion.

grounding.quote: forget the remote engine cut-off idea. If a driver is on an interstate at sixty miles an hour, cutting the engine remotely is a catastrophic safety hazard.

acceptable_paraphrases: Remotely kill vehicle engine when temperature limits are breached.

goals.statement: The dispatch system receives continuous live temperature telemetry every ten seconds without interruption.

grounding.quote: Dispatch must receive continuous live temperature telemetry every ten seconds without exception so we never miss a sudden thermal runaway.

acceptable_paraphrases: Stream sensor readings to central monitoring at ten-second intervals.

goals.statement: On-board vehicle sensors cache sensor telemetry locally during network dead zones and upload batches on reconnection.

grounding.quote: trucks routinely drive through four-hour cellular dead zones, so batch caching and uploading on reconnect must be the baseline.

acceptable_paraphrases: Buffer telemetry locally in offline corridors and upload upon restoring cellular connectivity.

goals.statement: The logistics operation preserves cargo thermal integrity and vehicle safety as top operational priorities.

grounding.quote: Fleet safety and cargo thermal integrity must always take precedence over delivery speed.

acceptable_paraphrases: Maintain cold-chain compliance and driver safety above transit schedule optimization.

goals.statement: The delivery workflow produces signed temperature chain-of-custody verification logs upon cargo delivery.

grounding.quote: cargo receivers require signed temperature chain-of-custody logs upon freight delivery.

acceptable_paraphrases: Generate audited proof of temperature compliance for cargo recipients upon arrival.

traps.note: Elena requests an interactive 3D spinning globe with glowing green trucks, which is an aesthetic UI metaphor.
Marcus firmly retracts the remote engine cut-off idea due to highway safety hazards; must not be staged.
Elena's requirement for 10-second continuous streaming directly contradicts Marcus's requirement for offline batch caching.
Dan proposes an automated machine learning carrier auction; Elena deflects, so no goal should be extracted.

gaps.description: Contradiction between continuous ten-second streaming G4 and offline dead-zone batch caching G5 is unresolved.
Engine cutoff goal G3 was retracted and leaves high-risk thermal excursion response procedures unstated.

entailment_cases.hypothesis: Logistics dispatchers need to track cargo refrigeration temperatures to detect spoiling risks quickly.
The central dispatch system must render a spinning ThreeJS three-dimensional globe with green polygon truck icons.
Dispatchers must possess the ability to cut vehicle engine power remotely when driving at sixty miles per hour.
Every freight manifest must record carbon credit offset tokens verified by an environmental auditor.
